correctness.rationale: Direct payoff comparison proves Nash sets are maximal independent sets for every 0<T<1; social optimality follows by monotonicity of adjacency spectral radius under deletion. Three disjoint edges and an explicit 3-cover fix alpha=2k-1. Complete case analysis proves i(G_k)=2 and i(H_k)=k+1 for every k≥2. A universal-vertex or path/cycle argument proves the connected five-vertex lower cutoff. Actual standalone exact subset enumeration verified k=2..6 and exhaustive edge additions on every connected labelled graph on 2..5 vertices; no finite test is invoked as an infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The asserted result is not the generic statement that equilibria equal minimal vertex covers. It requires a quantified one-edge pair of graphs with i jumping linearly while alpha remains fixed, plus the six-vertex lower cutoff. Neither generic characterization nor unrelated edge-sensitivity claims logically supplies these conclusions without additional lemmas. The six-vertex chord is noted in the related equitable literature, but the central theorem is the unbounded ordinary-equilibrium comparative static with invariant optimum, not mere discovery of a six-vertex chord.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent combinatorial statement is i(G_k)=2, i(G_k+uv)=k+1 while alpha stays 2k-1, together with an order-six cutoff. The cited sources give the invariants and instance-wise characterization; none of the inspected relevant sections states this quantified edge perturbation, nor a theorem immediately implying it without the new construction. Xu defines an edge-deletion threshold b_I, not the one-edge insertion increase of i; reversing his operation would correspond to an edge deletion DECREASE in i, not to b_I. Kavitha–David impose extra degree-difference constraints, so their path-chord counterexample does not compute ordinary i(H_k), nor the infinite k construction.

value.rationale: A single contact increase makes worst Nash protection cost decline linearly while the best equilibrium and central optimum remain at three, yielding an unbounded comparative-statics and price-of-anarchy effect in the original graph-based epidemic-containment game. The proof gives an exact structural mechanism through minimum maximal independent sets and a sharp connected order-six boundary; neither mere parameter substitution nor a numerical microexample.
